entities.summary:
Íñigo Dávalos was a Castilian general who served the Crown of Aragon in Italy.

Born in 1414 in Toledo, Spain, Dávalos rose through the ranks of the royal army to become a prominent military leader in the Mediterranean region. His expertise in warfare and diplomacy earned him the respect of his contemporaries and left a lasting legacy in the history of European military campaigns.

As a key figure in the Italian Wars, Dávalos played a crucial role in the siege of Naples and the Battle of Cerignola, contributing significantly to the Crown of Aragon's efforts to secure its territories in Southern Europe. His leadership and strategic thinking also influenced the development of modern warfare tactics.

Despite his military successes, Dávalos's life was marked by personal tragedy and loss. He died in 1484 at the age of 70, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most important Castilian generals of the Late Middle Ages.

"We must not forget the sacrifices of brave men like Íñigo Dávalos who fought for their kingdoms and their people," said King Ferdinand II of Aragon in a tribute to his fallen general.
